claim: A router contributor's July 2026 framework-design issue proposes explicitly naming 'in-tree plugins' as llm-d-router's 'supported surface' while treating 'out-of-tree plugins' as a real but only at-your-own-risk category, though this proposal remains unratified.
stance_target: maintainer/contributor position that out-of-tree plugin registration is not the officially supported pattern
scope_conditions: llm-d-router GitHub issue #2105, opened Jul 21 2026, status needs-triage/open/unresolved as of fetch (Sep 11 2026)
quoted_support: Documented at-your-own-risk: in-tree plugins are the supported surface; out-of-tree plugins that panic take the process down, stated loudly in the plugin developer docs.

claim: As of the issue's filing, llm-d-router's plugin framework has no panic recovery at any plugin invocation point, so a panicking plugin (in-tree or out-of-tree) kills the entire EPP process.
stance_target: risk profile of loading any external/out-of-tree plugin code into the EPP process
scope_conditions: llm-d-router EPP plugin framework as of Jul 2026
quoted_support: A panicking plugin kills the EPP process from any extension point; nothing recovers plugin invocations anywhere in the framework.

claim: llm-d-router issue #2105, opened Jul 21 2026 and still labeled needs-triage with zero comments as of fetch, proposes but has NOT ratified an 'unsupported-but-tolerated' out-of-tree plugin policy -- it is one of three competing options under open discussion, not a decided project stance.
stance_target: the framing that 'unsupported-but-tolerated' is the settled/recommended maintainer position on out-of-tree plugins
scope_conditions: GitHub issue tracker, llm-d/llm-d-router, as of fetch Sep 2026
